smt-2020-calculus-tiebreaker-01.title: Substitute $u=\ln x+\frac1x$
smt-2020-calculus-tiebreaker-01.body:
Rewrite $\frac{x-1}{x^2\ln x+x}=\frac{(x-1)/x^2}{\ln x+\frac1x}$. With $u=\ln x+\frac1x$ we have $du=\left(\frac1x-\frac1{x^2}\right)dx=\frac{x-1}{x^2}dx$. At $x=1$, $u=1$; at $x=2$, $u=\ln2+\frac12$. So the integral is $\int_1^{\ln2+1/2}\frac{du}u=\ln\left(\tfrac12+\ln2\right)$.

**Answer: $\ln\left(\frac12+\ln 2\right)$**

smt-2020-calculus-tiebreaker-02.title: Complex logarithm series
smt-2020-calculus-tiebreaker-02.body:
For $|z|=1$, $z\ne1$, $\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{z^n}n=-\ln(1-z)$ (convergent by Dirichlet's test and Abel's theorem). With $z=e^{i}$: $\sum\frac{\cos n}n=\operatorname{Re}(-\ln(1-e^i))=-\ln|1-e^i|=-\tfrac12\ln(2-2\cos1)$. And $\sum\frac{\sin n}n=\operatorname{Im}(-\ln(1-e^i))=-\arg(1-e^i)$. Now $1-e^{i}=-2i\sin\frac12\,e^{i/2}=2\sin\frac12\,e^{i(\frac12-\frac\pi2)}$, so $\arg(1-e^i)=\frac{1-\pi}2$ and $\sum\frac{\sin n}n=\frac{\pi-1}2$. Adding gives $\frac{\pi-1}2-\frac12\ln(2-2\cos1)$ ($\approx1.1128$).

**Answer: $\frac{\pi-1}{2}-\frac12\ln(2-2\cos 1)$**
